newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX edges up to new high of 3,818.21 pts.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX edges up to new high of 3,818.21 pts.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mixed with losers outnumbering gainers on Friday as Wall Street's overnight plunge left its imprint, traders said.
"Overall the market was bearish as the U.S. market left its impact on it," said Balazs Bathory of Creditansalt Securities. "This means investors are turning more cautious rather than disappearing."
Despite a bearish sentiment, the BUX index finished at a second successive high of 3,818.21 points, up 4.45 points, as a result of higher average prices in some heavy-weight issues.
The BUX index is calculated by average prices and sometimes does not accurately reflect trends based on closing prices.

The average price of OTP was 2,642 forints, compared to 2,579 on Thursday and it closed at 2,630, up 35. The average price of pharmaceuticals Egis was 8,873 forints, up from 8,839 and it closed at 8,830, down 20.
Spot share turnover reached a massive 2.06 billion forints.
"Turnover has been above two billion forints for the third successive day, that's quite a nice performance," Bathory said.
The recent change in trading rules allowing trading in all stocks simoultaneously during the whole session instead of in groups for limited periods has begun to bear fruit, Bathory said.
On Friday oil company MOL ended at 1,895 forints, down 20.
Pharmaceuticals Richter, alone generating a turnover of 1.1 billion forints turnover, finished at 8,875, down five.
Hotelier Danubius 's market went back to normal after euphory on Thursday. Danubius closed at 3,710, down 65.
